source: Yasunaga et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: The model is told to recall 3 to 5 relevant problems with solutions, then solve the new one, all in one prompt. No labeled data, no retrieval. It beat 0-shot CoT and often 3/5-shot CoT.
numbers: GSM8K columns 0-shot / 0-shot CoT / 5-shot CoT / analogical: GPT-3.5-turbo 75.0 / 75.8 / 76.7 / 77.8; text-davinci-003 14.8 / 50.3 / 54.0 / 61.0; PaLM2 60.8 / 78.2 / 80.7 / 81.7. MATH: GPT-3.5 33.0 / 33.9 / 34.9 / 37.3; PaLM2 27.1 / 29.8 / 34.3 / 34.8. K=5 exemplars for GSM8K, K=3 for MATH.
quote: Recall relevant problems before solving the new one
limits: On GSM8K with GPT-3.5 the gain over 0-shot CoT is only +2.0. Single run per cell, no confidence intervals. Benchmarks probably seen in pretraining.
agent_relevance: This is the S3 variant: one pass writes its own related problems. The effect is small on routine math, so do not count on it for easy classes.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (Codeforces)
finding: On hard code problems, adding self-generated knowledge (core algorithms) before the exemplars helped further.
numbers: Acc@1 / Acc@10. GPT-3.5-turbo-16k: 0-shot 8/24, 0-shot CoT 9/27, 3-shot CoT 11/27, self-exemplars 13/25, knowledge+exemplars 15/29. GPT-4: 16/30, 16/29, 17/31, 17/32, 19/37. 50 problems, run twice. Knowledge before exemplars 15/29 vs after 14/27.
limits: Only 50 Codeforces problems; 1 to 2 point gains on 50 items are inside noise. Acc@10 for self-exemplars alone (25) is below the 3-shot baseline (27).
agent_relevance: For hard problems, write the needed algorithm or concept first, then the analogues (knowledge, then exemplars).

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (BIG-Bench)
finding: On five BIG-Bench tasks with GPT-3.5-turbo, the method beat 0-shot CoT on all five and beat manual 3-shot CoT on four of five.
numbers: Columns 0-shot / 0-shot CoT / 3-shot CoT / analogical. Word sorting 66.8 / 67.6 / 68.4 / 75.2; logical deduction (5 objects) 30.0 / 35.2 / 36.4 / 41.6; temporal sequences 40.4 / 44.8 / 58.0 / 57.6; colored objects 50.4 / 61.6 / 62.0 / 68.0; formal fallacies 53.6 / 55.6 / 55.6 / 58.8.
limits: Five hand-picked tasks; no variance reported. On temporal sequences it ties rather than wins against 3-shot.
agent_relevance: Self-written analogues can replace hand-picked demos on structured tasks.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (scale and ablations)
finding: Self-generated exemplars only beat retrieved labeled exemplars when the model is strong. With small models retrieved real exemplars were better. Beyond K=3 more exemplars helped little; a diversity instruction helped; self-consistency stacked on top.
numbers: GSM8K by model: text-davinci-003 ours 61 vs retrieved 5-shot 57 vs fixed 5-shot 50; text-davinci-002 ours 48 vs retrieved 47; curie-001 and davinci-001 retrieved better. K=1: 76.1 GSM8K; K=3 to 5: 77.5 to 77.8. Diverse 77.8 / 37.3 vs non-diverse 75.9 / 35.2. Ours plus self-consistency 85.3 GSM8K / 46.0 MATH.
limits: Scale threshold: the method fails when the model cannot write valid problems. The self-consistency gain (+7.5 on GSM8K) dwarfs the analogical gain (+2).
agent_relevance: Gate O7 and S3 analogue writing by model strength. Majority voting beats analogue writing per unit of effort on routine math.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (manual error analysis)
finding: Authors hand-checked 100 outputs (50 right, 50 wrong). Many self-written exemplars were flawed even when the final answer was right.
numbers: Right answers: 35/50 relevant and correct exemplars, 9/50 relevant but wrong solutions, 6/50 irrelevant. Wrong answers: 28/50 good exemplars but the model still failed (12 generalization gap, 8 over-reliance on one exemplar, 8 other), 12/50 relevant but wrong solutions, 10/50 irrelevant.
limits: Small sample, mixed GSM8K and MATH, authors' own annotation.
agent_relevance: Self-written analogues are wrong or off target in roughly 40 percent of cases. Any analogue step needs its solution checked (G10: reasoning text is not evidence).

source: Qin et al. (2025, ACL) Relevant or Random: Can LLMs Truly Perform Analogical Reasoning?
finding: Direct test of the claim that relevance drives the gain. Self-generated random or irrelevant examples did as well or better on math. What mattered was the accuracy of the generated examples.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo, 3 seeds. GSM8K: relevant 71.5, N/A (no type given) 75.5, random-same-domain 75.1, random-different 76.3, random-biology 75.3. MATH: relevant 33.3, N/A 36.1, 36.3, 34.1, 34.6. Math average: relevant 52.4 vs 54.9 to 55.8 for irrelevant. On five BBH tasks the pattern flipped: relevant averaged 63.2, the best arm (row order as extracted; N/A 61.9, random-biology 61.7, random-same 60.4, random-different 56.4). Abstract: +4 on GSM8K with random biology examples.
quote: self-generated random examples can surprisingly achieve comparable or even better performance
limits: Mainly GPT-3.5 (GPT-4o-mini and Llama noted). Their relevant arm on GSM8K (71.5) is below the original paper's GPT-3.5 figures (77.8), so prompt wording differs. Relevance only helped on BBH.
agent_relevance: The analogue gain may be mostly a self-generated few-shot format effect. Do not credit analogy for a gain without a random-example control.

source: Qin et al. (2025) Relevant or Random (mechanism)
finding: Relevant self-generated MATH problems were harder and more often wrong. Accuracy of the examples tracked performance. Replacing the answers with GPT-4 answers helped.
numbers: Hand-checked accuracy of generated MATH examples (50 per type): relevant 62%, N/A 72%, random-same 86%. Mean cosine similarity of relevant examples to query: BBH 0.46, math 0.48. GPT4-calibration beat plain ICL for every arm (e.g. GSM8K relevant 71.2 to 75.2).
limits: Hand check on 50 problems per arm. It does not show relevance is useless, only that its cost in accuracy outweighs the benefit on math.
agent_relevance: Relevance and correctness trade off: closer analogues are harder and less often right. Verify analogue answers by code or a second model.

source: Qin et al. (2025) Relevant or Random (new methods)
finding: Two cheap variants: generate a few random math or biology problems once, check them, reuse as fixed demos for every query. They matched or beat per-query generation at much lower cost.
numbers: GSM8K / MATH / average: ICL-math 75.7 / 36.8 / 56.3; ICL-bio 77.9 / 34.9 / 56.4; relevant analogical prompting 71.5 / 33.3 / 52.4. Fixed set generated once.
limits: GPT-3.5 only for these; no tests on reasoning-trained models.
agent_relevance: A stored bank of vetted worked examples is cheaper than regenerating per query; this fits the memory layer.

source: Gwak et al. (2026) Not the Example, but the Process: How Self-Generated Examples Enhance LLM Reasoning
finding: Splits the effect. Integrated: the model writes a related problem and solves it inside the same prompt. Decoupled: the same generated problems pasted as examples with the creation step removed. The gain comes from the act of creating, not from the example text.
numbers: Five models (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, Gemini-1.5-Flash, Llama-3.3-70B, Llama-3.1-8B). GPT-4o GSM8K: zero-shot 49.89, integrated 54.59, decoupled 50.49. GPT-4o MATH: 33.33, 37.86, 32.65. Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K: 12.06, 16.49, 11.60. Llama-3.3-70B MATH: zero-shot 33.59, integrated 35.19, decoupled 33.59 (Table 1 as extracted). Attention: integrated attends more to generated example tokens (p < 1e-10, paired t-test); decoupled attends more to the test question.
quote: the key benefit arises not from the generated examples themselves but from the act of creating them
limits: Greedy decoding. Absolute GSM8K scores are low for these models, so the prompt format is probably restrictive. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence for writing the analogue inside the live reasoning, not as a stored artefact. Pasted analogues give about zero gain, which fits the schema's warning that unaided analogy rarely transfers.

source: Kim et al. (2022) Self-Generated In-Context Learning (SG-ICL)
finding: Earliest form of the idea: the model writes its own demonstrations for each class from the test input, then does in-context learning. Worth about 0.6 gold samples, with lower variance than random gold demos.
numbers: Four text classification tasks, GPT-J 6B scale models. Abstract: SG-ICL 'worth approximately 0.6 gold training samples'. Lower variance across demo draws than randomly selected gold demos.
limits: Small classification tasks and a small model; not reasoning problems. Self-generated demos are weaker than real gold demos on average.
agent_relevance: Predecessor of O7 analogue writing. The variance reduction is the more reliable benefit than the mean gain.

source: Zhang et al. (2022/2023, ICLR) Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models (Auto-CoT)
finding: Builds demonstrations with the model: cluster questions, take one per cluster, write the chain with 'Let's think step by step'. Found that similarity-retrieved demos can hurt because their wrong chains mislead the model.
numbers: GPT-3, Table 3: MultiArith Zero-shot-CoT 78.7, Manual-CoT 91.7, Auto-CoT 92.0; GSM8K 40.7 / 46.9 / 47.9; AQuA 33.5 / 35.8 / 36.5; Coin flip 91.4 / 97.2 / 99.9. Table 1: Retrieval-Q-CoT 82.8 vs Random-Q-CoT 86.2 on MultiArith (retrieval lost); with gold chains on GSM8K 48.0 vs 47.6 and AQuA 39.7 vs 36.2 (retrieval won). Codex: Auto-CoT 62.8 vs Manual 59.4 on GSM8K but 93.2 vs 96.8 on MultiArith.
limits: Differences mostly under 2 points; Auto-CoT averaged over only three runs.
agent_relevance: Warning for O7: the most similar examples carry the same errors; diversity protects. Same lesson as Qin: unverified similar analogues mislead.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
finding: Zero-shot CoT ('Let's think step by step') is the baseline that analogical prompting is compared against.
numbers: text-davinci-002: MultiArith 17.7 to 78.7, GSM8K 10.4 to 40.7 (abstract).
quote: increasing the accuracy on MultiArith from 17.7% to 78.7%
limits: Large gains appear on older models; modern instruction-tuned models already reason step by step, which shrinks both the CoT and the analogical gain.
agent_relevance: Any gain claimed for O7 must be measured over zero-shot CoT, not over a plain prompt.

source: Zheng et al. (2024, ICLR) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in Large Language Models
finding: Sister method: first ask a higher-level question about the principle behind the problem, then solve. Larger and more consistent gains than analogical prompting on knowledge-heavy tasks.
numbers: PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4 to 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 to 81.8 (5 runs each). GPT-4: Physics 69.4 to 84.5, Chemistry 80.9 to 85.6; zero-shot CoT on GPT-4 gave 82.9 and 85.3. TimeQA +27 points for PaLM-2L (with retrieval 68.7%). MuSiQue 35.5 to 42.8, StrategyQA 82.8 to 86.4 (PaLM-2L). On MMLU Physics it fixed 20.5% of baseline errors and added 11.9% new errors.
limits: On GPT-4 plain CoT is almost as good (82.9 vs 84.5 Physics). Authors say reasoning, not abstraction, remains the main error source.
agent_relevance: Abstraction (principle first) is a cheap alternative or companion to analogue writing at S2 and S3, with stronger evidence.

source: Chen et al. (2023, ACL) Self-ICL: Zero-Shot In-Context Learning with Self-Generated Demonstrations
finding: Model writes 3 pseudo-inputs, labels them zero-shot, then uses them as demos. It beat zero-shot on average over 23 BIG-Bench Hard tasks but with real harm on some tasks.
numbers: InstructGPT (text-davinci-003) all-task average: ZS-Direct 50.81 to Self-ICL 53.93 (+3.12); ZS-CoT 53.22 to 55.54 (+2.32); real 3-shot 55.49. Win-tie-lose vs ZS-Direct 18-0-5, vs ZS-CoT 16-2-5. Temporal sequences -22.0, logical deduction 7 objects -3.6. gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct: average +1.20, causal judgement fell 42.25 to 12.30. text-bison-001 average +1.05.
quote: SELF-ICL outperforms zero-shot baselines on both average accuracy and head-to-head comparison
limits: Tasks where the model writes malformed pseudo-inputs show large drops. Gains are small on strong chat models.
agent_relevance: Same shape as analogical prompting: small average gain, large per-task variance with real losses. Needs a per-task gate (G12) and a validity check on the made-up examples.

source: Yu et al. (2024, ICLR) Thought Propagation: An Analogical Approach to Complex Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Agent-style analogy: propose analogous problems, solve them, then reuse their results or plans to amend the first answer. It beat IO, CoT, BaG and Tree of Thoughts on three tasks.
numbers: Shortest-path optimal rate, 0-shot: GPT-3.5 IO 0.33, CoT 0.26, ToT 0.22, TP 0.65; GPT-4 IO 0.78, ToT 0.46, TP 0.88; PaLM-2 IO 0.14, TP 0.36. Creative writing (100 prompts) GPT-4 coherence IO 6.19, ToT 7.68, TP 7.99; human preference TP 45% vs ToT 33%. ALFWorld (134 tasks) overall success: ReAct avg 57, Reflexion 79.1, TP variants 83.68 to 94.78.
limits: Authors reproduce Reflexion themselves; others quoted from ReAct. 1-layer TP costs about the same tokens as ToT, 2-layer more. ToT falling below IO in their shortest-path setup suggests a weak baseline.
agent_relevance: Closest published method to O7 inside an agent loop: analogous problems are solved first, then their solutions amend the original. Compare token cost before adopting.

source: Webb, Holyoak and Lu (2023, Nature Human Behaviour) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Zero-shot GPT-3 matched or beat undergraduates on text matrices, letter-string, verbal and SAT analogies. It did worse than people on story analogies (far condition).
numbers: Digit Matrices: GPT-3 above human average (N=40 UCLA), generative OR = 1.88, p = .005; multiple choice OR = 6.27, p = 2.3e-8. Letter strings human N=57; verbal analogies N=57 (UCLA VAT), N=20 (Sternberg and Nigro); SAT analogies above estimated average high-school level; semantic distance effect OR = 3.24. Story analogies (N=54): humans beat GPT-3 (OR = 0.37, p = .0003); GPT-3 not significant in far condition (p = .065); GPT-4 near perfect on near analogies.
limits: Model was GPT-3 (text-davinci-003). The 'emergent' claim was challenged by counterfactual tests (Lewis and Mitchell).
agent_relevance: Models can map structure when the analogy is given. The harder step is finding a far analogue, which is the step analogical prompting leaves to the model.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Using Counterfactual Tasks to Evaluate the Generality of Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Re-ran Webb's letter-string analogies with permuted or symbol alphabets. Humans stayed high; GPT-3, 3.5 and 4 dropped sharply.
numbers: Humans: 136 Prolific participants, two random alphabets from permutation levels n in {0,2,5,10,20}. For each n, 7 alphabets with 10 problems each were built. GPT accuracy fell as permutation grew while human accuracy stayed high.
quote: the GPT models' performance declines sharply on the counterfactual set
limits: Letter-string only. Per-model accuracies are in figures that I could not extract as text.
agent_relevance: Model analogy depends on familiar surface forms. For far or unfamiliar domains a model's self-made analogues may be pattern retrieval, so require an explicit mapping check (O7 mapping step).

source: Hu et al. (2023) In-Context Analogical Reasoning with Pre-Trained Language Models
finding: Describing Raven's matrix features in words let language models do zero-shot analogy, exceeding human averages. Higher-level abstractions helped further.
numbers: RAVEN sub-task Center: GPT-3 36.8% to 69.2% under more abstract encodings (up to 95.6% under the best listed); OPT 125M 22.2 to 45.6; OPT 1.3B 47.2 and up.
limits: Perceptual features were given in text by the experimenter, so perception is not tested.
agent_relevance: Re-encoding a task as relations in plain words can unlock analogy. S2 REPRESENT should write relations in words.

source: Jiayang et al. (2023, EMNLP) AnalogyKB: Unlocking Analogical Reasoning of Language Models with A Million-scale Knowledge Base
finding: Million-scale analogy knowledge base built from knowledge graphs (same-relation and meta-relation analogies). Fine-tuning small LMs on it improved analogy tasks.
numbers: Abstract level: over one million analogies; improvements on analogy benchmarks; task numbers not extracted.
limits: Training-based, not prompt-only. I did not extract task numbers.
agent_relevance: Shows analogy data can be built from graphs by code (typed mapping) rather than from model memory.

source: Choi et al. (2024, EMNLP) AnaloBench: Benchmarking the Identification of Abstract and Long-context Analogies
finding: The hard part for models is finding the right analogue in a large pool and handling long stories. Scale did not fix it.
numbers: T1 accuracy at 1, 10, 30 sentences: GPT-4 89.1, 66.5, 60.7; GPT-3.5 65.3, 46.4, 30.8; Claude 68.2, 30.2, 25.9; humans 96.0, 72.5, 73.3. Retrieval of analogous stories from a bank: GPT-4-Turbo near the random baseline for longer stories. 340 human-written analogies, 12 open and 3 proprietary models.
limits: Stories extended by GPT-4 (checked with Claude-written stories, little change).
agent_relevance: Recall of far analogues from a large pool is weak, so O7 should use small indexed stores or code-side retrieval, not model recall from a long context.

source: Lee et al. (2025) The Curious Case of Analogies: Investigating Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Mechanistic probing: models encode the relation in mid-upper layers when right, but often fail to apply it to the new entity. Successes show strong structural alignment between source and target.
numbers: Proportional and story analogies. Failures: missing relation information in the layers, or poor application. Patching hidden states at key tokens helped to a certain extent. Alignment score separates successes from failures.
limits: Open models only; I did not capture accuracy deltas.
agent_relevance: Two failure routes: relation never extracted, or extracted but not applied. A mapping step that states the relation in words and then applies it covers both.

source: Jiang and Merlo (2026) Analogical Structure, Minimal Contextual Cues and Contrastive Distractors: Input Design for Sample-Efficient Linguistic Rule Induction
finding: Organising training input as analogical paradigms drove sample efficiency for small models, while prompted LLMs needed far more data to match them.
numbers: English verb alternation tasks. Lightweight models trained on hundreds to one thousand examples reached higher F1 than zero- and few-shot LLMs. Ablation: analogical organisation was the main driver.
limits: Authors say it compares learning regimes, not a verdict on LLMs. Narrow linguistic task.
agent_relevance: Laying out paired contrast cases side by side is a useful way to present examples at S2.

source: Shen, Druckmann and Zou (2026) Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
finding: Open-ended solution generation: an analogical reasoning pipeline (cross-domain analogies by shared relational structure, then search for solutions) reduced mode collapse.
numbers: Diversity metrics up 90 to 173%; novel solutions over 50% of the time versus as low as 1.6% for baselines; 13-fold gain on distributional metrics for perturbation prediction; state of the art on 2 oligonucleotide datasets; Spearman 0.729 on brain-region interaction.
limits: Preprint. Novelty judged by authors' metrics; four biomedical case studies.
agent_relevance: Supports the schema's open mode: far analogues raise spread and belong at open-mode S3, not on routine problems (O7 variance note).

source: Euclid-geometry study (2025/2026) Reliable Proof Generation with LLMs via Analogical Retrieval and Symbolic Verification
finding: Retrieved analogous problems and their proofs, plus a formal verifier giving feedback. The verifier gave much of the lift; analogy added a further, controlled gain.
numbers: SAT-level geometry. Full pipeline 68 to 96% versus 10 to 44% for LLM-only. With the same verifier and budget, analogical guidance raised GPT-5 88 to 96, Claude Sonnet 4.6 78 to 86, Gemini-Flash-2.5 72 to 86, OpenAI o1 52 to 80. 50-problem ablation: Gemini-2.5-Flash and Claude Sonnet 4.6, analogy-derived setup reached 86% with retries versus 72 to 78% for random examples and 22% single-run baseline.
limits: Small sets (50 problems in ablation); geometry only; retrieval uses symbolic features, not model recall.
agent_relevance: Best match to our design: analogue found by code, mapping checked by a verifier. The analogue step helps when a checker exists.

source: Lin et al. (2024) Self-Demos: Eliciting Out-of-Demonstration Generalizability in Large Language Models
finding: Query-aware demo generation: the model writes demos that sit between the given demos and a query that is out of distribution. Reported gains on a tool-use set and two math sets.
numbers: OOD-Toolset: over 300 real APIs and 1000 instances, three tool-use demos plus one out-of-demonstration query each. Math sets: GSM8K with manually created outliers (1,319 items) and MATH with same level, different subject (1,000 items). Accuracy cells not extracted.
limits: Comparisons depend on the authors' own OOD set construction.
agent_relevance: A tool-using agent can generate bridge demos for an unseen tool call at S3.

source: Singhal and Singhal (2025) Analogy-Driven Financial Chain-of-Thought (AD-FCoT)
finding: Prompts the model to recall historical events with known outcomes, then reasons by CoT on new news. Reports higher sentiment accuracy and better correlation with returns than zero-shot, few-shot, role and domain CoT prompts.
numbers: FNSPID news published after the model's training cutoff (to avoid look-ahead bias), thousands of articles. Exact accuracies not extracted.
limits: Two-author preprint; direction of effect only.
agent_relevance: A domain where the analogue is a past case with a known outcome that can be checked.

source: Chen et al. (2025) DeFine: Decision-Making with Analogical Reasoning over Factor Profiles
finding: Builds probabilistic factor profiles from earnings-call transcripts and retrieves analogous past scenarios to guide decisions.
numbers: Abstract level: improves decisions over verbose transcripts via analogous scenarios; figures not extracted.
limits: Finance domain; analogues come from retrieval over past transcripts, not model recall.
agent_relevance: Pairs a structured profile (typed mapping) with retrieved analogues, close to O7 with a code-checked mapping.
